data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Decentralized networks are fundamentally less resilient because they suffer from 'fragmented fragility', where the lack of total redundancy at any single node increases the frequency of partial outages.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The 'fragmented fragility' is offset by the fact that no single outage ever reaches the scale of a total system collapse.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Small services are significantly easier to restart and recover than a monolithic large service.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"While a large service avoids frequent small outages through massive over-provisioning, a decentralized network of small services operates closer to their capacity limits. This creates a state of 'constant low-level churn' where the system is always partially failed, reducing the overall quality of service compared to a robust, unified entity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
